rhs_question_text: A school is choosing a method for repeatedly sorting small lists of TEN assessment scores. Discuss BUBBLE, INSERTION and MERGE SORT. Compare how they work, their best/average/worst time and space complexities, and argue which is most suitable when a list is small or already nearly sorted. [12]
rhs_answer_points_draft: Bubble swaps adjacent out-of-order values over passes; early-exit optimised bubble can be O(n) best but O(n²) average/worst. Insertion grows an ordered prefix, O(n) best and O(n²) average/worst, with O(1) auxiliary space. Merge recursively divides and recombines ordered sublists in O(n log n) across typical cases, generally needing O(n) extra array storage. For ten values constants and simplicity can favour insertion or bubble, while merge scales better to much larger inputs.
rhs_marking_rule_draft: Teacher-marked 12-mark holistic levels: detailed applied evaluation 9–12; sound 5–8; basic 1–4; none 0. Do not claim merge is always fastest for tiny inputs.
